Subject: Post-call recap: tool/function calling patterns (SDK, auth, routing, embeddings)

Alex / Samir —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery call so we can keep momentum on the FinApps integration:

Highlights from the call:
- Primary use case: contextual augmentation for financial document Q&A + automated reconciliation workflows.
- Expected QPS: initial pilot ~15 req/s, target production 80–120 req/s (bursty at month-end).
- Latency SLO: p95 at <500ms for user-facing queries; background jobs can be higher.
- Data sensitivity: PII in documents; FinApps needs private deployment (VPC) and KMS integration.

Integration / architecture topics we covered (and proposed patterns):
1) SDK setup & auth
   - Recommend server-side SDK for calls that access customer data; use service tokens paired with short-lived session tokens for client features.
   - We support OIDC + mTLS for Private deployments; sample config included in attached diagram.

2) Routing & model selection
   - Use request metadata to route: low-latency interactive -> smaller tuned model; batch re-ranker/embeddings -> larger quantized model.
   - Fallback policy: if Dedicated capacity is saturated, route to hosted variant with identical API surface but different cost profile.

3) Structured output & tool calling
   - Recommend schema-first tool definitions for function calling (JSON schema) for: 1) document retrieval, 2) ledger reconciliation, 3) external system write (webhook).
   - For critical operations (writes), require explicit confirmation step with signed event.

4) Embeddings + reranker pattern
   - Hybrid approach: store coarse embeddings for candidate retrieval; run a reranker model (or prompt-based rerank) over top-N retrieved docs.
   - Cache reranker outputs for repeated queries; TTL based on document change events.

5) Parallel tools & error handling
   - Parallelize independent tool calls (e.g., call vendor-sentiment API and internal data fetch in parallel) and reconcile results.
   - For partial failures, surface deterministic error codes and fall back to best-effort single-source answers with clear provenance.

Attachments:
- redwood-integration-arch.pdf (high-level flow + auth samples)
- mutual-action-plan.xlsx (timeline + owners)

Next steps / ask:
1) Technical deep-dive: schedule 60m working session with Dev (cc'd) next week to walk the architecture diagram and exchange sample telemetry.
2) Security checklist: please share FinApps SOC2/HIPAA scope doc so our security team can map controls.
3) Pilot scope: confirm target dataset (sample 10–20k docs) and pilot success criteria (latency, UAT pass rate).

I can host the deep-dive Wed or Thu (10–2 PT). Let me know what works for you.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Alex —

Great questions, answers inline below. Also re-attached the diagram and updated the Drive link.

1) Mapping existing APIs to tool definitions
   - We usually run a short API-mapping workshop (1.5–2h) with your platform/infra team to: inventory endpoints, identify canonical operations (read vs write), and propose canonical tool schemas.
   - For edge cases, we wrap legacy endpoints with a thin adapter that normalizes inputs/outputs to the tool schema. That adapter can be deployed as a Lambda or small service.

2) Reranker CPU fallback
   - Yes — you can run a lightweight CPU-based reranker for low-traffic periods or non-interactive requests. Expect 2–5x higher latency vs optimized GPU reranker depending on model size; quality can be comparable if you use a smaller architecture fine-tuned for ranking.
   - Recommendation: 1) GPU for p95-sensitive interactive flows; 2) CPU fallback for background reprocessing and nightly batches.

3) Diagram access
   - Fixed. New link: https://drive.company/redwood-integration-arch (public link with expiration). Also re-attached PDF to this email.

- Lock deep-dive: Wed 21 Apr 2027, 10:00–11:00 PT (invite to follow).

- Security intake: FinApps to share SOC2 scope doc by Apr 23; Redwood security will provide a readout within 3 business days.
